In [[mathematics]], the '''antilimit''' is the equivalent of a [[Limit (mathematics)|limit]] for a [[divergent series]]. The concept is not necessarily unique or well-defined, but the general idea is to find a formula for a series and then evaluate it outside its [[radius of convergence]].

== Common divergent series ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Series !! Antilimit
|-
| [[1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + ⋯]] || -1/2
|-
| [[Grandi's series|1 − 1 + 1 − 1 + ⋯ (Grandi's series)]] || 1/2
|-
| [[1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + ⋯]] || -1/12
|-
| [[1 − 2 + 3 − 4 + ⋯]] || 1/4
|-
| [[1 − 1 + 2 − 6 + 24 − 120 + …]] || 0.59634736...
|-
| [[1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ⋯]] || -1
|-
| [[1 − 2 + 4 − 8 + ⋯]] || 1/3
|-
| [[Harmonic series (mathematics)|1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + ⋯ (harmonic series)]] || <math> \gamma </math>
|}
